gates.title: Vector Algebra operations demanded by selected ExamSIDE PYQs

canonical_concepts.statement: A nonzero vector divided by its magnitude preserves direction and becomes a unit vector.
The dot product is a scalar encoding alignment and projection; for nonzero vectors it is zero at perpendicularity.
The cross product is an ordered axial vector perpendicular to the input plane and reverses under operand swap.

external_prerequisites.statement: Recover a reference angle from a valid trigonometric ratio.

relations.expression: |A| = sqrt(Ax^2 + Ay^2 + Az^2); A_hat = A/|A|; tan(theta_ref)=|Ay/Ax|
relations.meaning: Cartesian components determine vector magnitude and normalized direction; in two dimensions a reference angle is placed in the physical quadrant using component signs.
conditions: The i/j/k basis is orthonormal.
|A| is nonzero before A_hat=A/|A| is formed.
For a 2D direction angle, component signs are retained to place the inverse-trig reference angle in the physical quadrant.

relations.expression: A·B = AxBx + AyBy + AzBz = |A||B| cos(theta); proj_B(A) = (A·B/|B|^2) B
relations.meaning: The dot product links Cartesian components to angle and supplies perpendicularity and projection tests.
conditions: A and B are expressed in the same orthonormal Cartesian basis.
The angle form requires nonzero magnitudes for both vectors.
The vector projection formula requires |B| nonzero.

relations.meaning: The cross product is an axial vector perpendicular to A and B; magnitude gives parallelogram area and orientation follows the right-hand rule.
conditions: A and B are expressed in one right-handed orthonormal i/j/k basis.
The magnitude relation uses the smaller angle theta between the vector directions.
Right-hand orientation is applied to the ordered pair A then B; reversing the order reverses the result.

validity_conditions: Keep scalar dot output distinct from axial cross output.
Direction recovery from inverse trig remains quadrant-aware.

reasoning_sequence.action: Write vectors/components in one basis and identify requested output type.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Operation choice depends on the requested scalar/vector geometry.

reasoning_sequence.action: Apply the corresponding unit/dot/cross relation preserving signs and operand order.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Each relation encodes a different invariant and output type.

reasoning_sequence.action: Use normalization, symmetry or perpendicularity to verify.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Dot and cross products are notation choices for the same combination.
misconceptions.counterexample: A·B is scalar and symmetric; A×B is axial and reverses under operand swap.
misconceptions.repair: Name requested output and invariant before choosing the operation.

problem_families.title: Selected unit/dot/cross Vector Algebra questions
hidden_invariants: Cross product is perpendicular and anti-commutative.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from the first symbol of the first relation.

gates.title: Applied NLM relations demanded by selected ExamSIDE PYQs

canonical_concepts.statement: A friction coefficient supplies a state-dependent bound/model; static friction is not automatically limiting.
Equal tension and linked acceleration claims are conditional on the stated ideal connection model.
Average force is momentum change per unit time; repeated identical changes create an average momentum-flow force.

relations.expression: 0 <= f_s <= mu_s N; f_s,max = mu_s N; f_k = mu_k N
relations.meaning: Static friction adjusts up to a limit; once the kinetic model applies, friction magnitude is mu_k N.
conditions: The contact pair and relative sliding/tendency have been identified first.
The normal reaction N belongs to the same contact and current force state.
Use f_s=mu_s N only at impending slip; otherwise static friction may be smaller.
Use f_k=mu_k N only when the adopted kinetic-friction model applies during sliding.

relations.expression: T is equal along one massless string over a smooth fixed pulley; connected endpoints have equal acceleration magnitude along the string constraint
relations.meaning: In the stated ideal-string/smooth-pulley model, tension is uniform and inextensibility links endpoint motions.
conditions: The string is massless and inextensible.
The pulley is smooth and fixed unless the problem states a different geometry.
Tension equality is asserted only along the same continuous ideal string.
Acceleration relation follows the actual string-length constraint and may involve opposite signed directions even when magnitudes match.

relations.expression: p = m v; J = Delta p = F_avg Delta t; F_avg = Delta p/Delta t
relations.meaning: Momentum change equals impulse; average force equals momentum change per time, including repeated-item momentum transfer.
conditions: Momentum and velocity refer to the same chosen body/item and inertial frame.
F_avg is the average net force associated with the stated momentum change over Delta t.
For repeated-item momentum flow, the item momentum change and item rate are defined over the same steady counting interval.

validity_conditions: Use ideal string/pulley equalities only under declared model.
Momentum-rate force is tied to a stated interval or steady item rate.

reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The quantitative relation is conditional on the physical model.

reasoning_sequence.action: Write friction, connected-body or momentum-rate relation with Newton-II body equations as needed.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Extension relations supplement rather than replace body-specific mechanics.
A solved result can still violate the assumed contact/connection model.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Every coefficient/string/rate number can be inserted into an automatic formula before checking state.
misconceptions.counterexample: Static friction can be below mu_sN; nonideal pulleys can have unequal tensions; momentum becomes force only through time.
misconceptions.repair: State contact/connection/time model before selecting equality.

problem_families.title: Selected friction, pulley and momentum-rate questions
hidden_invariants: Static friction obeys a bound before the limit.
Each connected body keeps its own force equation.
Average force is momentum change per time.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from the first symbol of the first relation.
